hero.heading: What this component does
hero.description: A visual representation of a user or entity, shown as a photo, initials, or icon, with an optional status indicator. Nine sizes step from xxxsmall to xxxlarge with medium as the base, and the badges, ring and glyphs all scale from that step. The status badge carries a distinct glyph per state as well as its colour. Content type isn't an exposed property, swap the nested Avatar Type instance directly to change it. For a notification count on an icon or nav item, use the Notification Indicator component instead, Avatar's own indicator is for presence, not counts.

rows.Description: The smallest step, for dense inline contexts like compact tables or comment threads. The presence glyph is only a few pixels across here, so do not rely on anyone reading it.
A step up from xxxsmall, still compact, for dense lists.
For secondary avatars in tight layouts, like a stacked group of collaborators.
For list rows and menu items where the avatar sits alongside text.
The base step, and a balanced general-purpose choice for cards and list headers. Every other size is scaled from it, so start here unless something specific argues otherwise.
For emphasis in a card header or a comment's author avatar.
For a prominent single avatar, like a user menu or account switcher.
For profile headers where the avatar is a focal point.
The largest step, for full profile pages or standalone display. The close glyph does not grow with its badge at this size, so check it still reads as a target.
Shows a dismiss badge pinned to the top-right corner. Use in removable contexts, like a multi-select chip list.
Hides the dismiss badge. The default for most read-only contexts where the avatar isn't removable.

Shows a presence badge pinned to the bottom-right corner, defaulting to Available. The badge is an exposed instance, so its state is reachable in the properties panel without detaching or hunting for the nested layer.
Hides the presence badge. Use when presence doesn't apply, like a generic entity avatar or a purely illustrative photo.
Shows a border/default outline ring around the avatar, weight scales with Size.
Hides the ring. Use on backgrounds where the outline competes with surrounding content.

The person is reachable now. It is the default, so an avatar whose presence never updates will keep claiming availability it cannot back up. Turn Show Status off rather than leaving a stale Available.
Signed in but idle. Only use it where the system can actually detect idleness, otherwise it reads as a guess the viewer will trust.
Reachable but occupied. It describes the person, where DND describes what their notifications are doing, so the two are not interchangeable.
Notifications are suppressed by the person's own choice. Use it only when something really is being suppressed, because it tells the viewer a message may never surface.
Working a scheduled shift, for rota-based contexts. Outside a shift-based product it reads as a second word for Available and dilutes both.
Not reachable. It is the one state drawn as a hollow badge rather than a filled one, so it stays tellable apart when colour is unreliable.

Not a presence state. It is a dismiss mark that happens to live in the same component, and Avatar already uses it for the top-right badge. Setting the bottom-right Status to Close puts two dismiss marks on one avatar.
Hands the glyph over to the Custom Icon property for a meaning outside the presence set. Everything a viewer has learned from the other seven states stops applying, so reach for it rarely.

Takes effect only while Status is Icon, where it replaces the built-in glyph. The suggested list holds just the Star set, though any component can be swapped in. A custom glyph carries none of the shared meaning the named states have, so it needs a text equivalent beside it.

rows.What changes: Avatar has no hover, pressed, or focus states in Figma. Close and Status are static badges that change only with the Status property, so whatever click behaviour Close has in a real interface lives in code rather than here.

rows.Description: None modeled in Figma. Avatar is presented as a static graphic, any transition when swapping Size, content, or toggling Show Close, Show Status, or Show Ring lives in code.
Initials, photo, or icon. Not an exposed property, swap the nested Avatar Type instance directly to change it.
Background color behind initials or an icon (purple, blue, sea, yellow, orange, green, burgundy, using chart/series tokens). Not used behind a photo. Swap the nested Swatch instance directly.
Used only when Content type is photo, fills the circle. In Figma swap the nested Photo instance to any of the named photos in _Avatar Photos. In code any image can be passed as an image property.

Holds one of eight states from the _Status Indicator component, each drawn with its own glyph from the Assets library. The instance is exposed, so the state is set from Avatar's own properties panel without detaching. Only rendered while Show Status is true.
The glyph used while Status is Icon. Any component can be swapped in and the suggested list holds only the Star set, so nothing constrains it to a presence-shaped mark.

sections.title: Anatomy
rawTextContent: Fills the frame, auto-positioned. Holds initials with a colored swatch, a photo, or an icon with a colored swatch. Not an exposed property, swap the nested instance directly
An absolute-positioned outline matching the frame's edges. border/default color, stroke only. Weight scales proportionally with Size, 2px at medium
Pinned to the top-right corner. An instance of the Status Indicator component's Close variant, shown or hidden with Show Close
Pinned to the bottom-right corner, defaults to Available. Shown or hidden with Show Status. The instance is exposed, so its state, and for the Icon state its glyph, are reachable directly.

sections.title: How to use
dos: Match Size to context, dense lists and tables call for the smaller sizes (xxxsmall to small), profile headers and standalone display call for the larger ones (xlarge to xxxlarge).
Turn off Show Status for generic entities or purely illustrative photos where presence doesn't apply.
donts: Don't use the presence Status badge for unread or notification counts, that's a different purpose, use the Notification Indicator component instead.

sections.title: Accessibility & Content Guidelines
items: Purely visual, an avatar image or initials alone don't convey a name, pair it with visible text or provide an accessible name in code

Each presence state now carries its own glyph as well as its colour, so the badge no longer depends on colour alone. Still give it a text equivalent, because at the smallest sizes the glyph is only a few pixels across
The Close badge implies a dismiss action, give it an accessible name in code like "Remove [name]", Figma has no interactive state for it
The close glyph is drawn at a fixed size whatever the avatar, so on the largest avatars it sits very small inside its badge. Check it still reads as a target

rows.Type: Fixed per Size, medium is the base
rows.Description: Nine fixed squares stepping 24, 32, 36, 40, 48, 64, 80, 120 and 200px, with medium at 48px as the base. Medium is the only step bound to a token (control/lg), every other step is an authored value. Not resizable independently of the Size property.

rows.Type: Scales with Size, medium is the base
rows.Description: The Status and Close badges are 16px at medium, exactly one third of the avatar, and step 8, 10, 12, 12, 16, 18, 24, 36 and 56px across the ladder. Above medium they grow more slowly than the avatar, so a large avatar is never dominated by its badge.

The status glyph holds a constant share of its badge at every size, 0.42 of the badge width, so it stays proportional from 24px through 200px. The close glyph is drawn at a fixed 5px at every size, so its share of the badge falls from two thirds at xxxsmall to under a tenth at xxxlarge.

rows.Type: Scales per Size tier, medium is the base
rows.Description: 2px (stroke/thick) at medium and every step below it, 4px (stroke/heavy) at large and xlarge, then 6px and 8px at xxlarge and xxxlarge. The two heaviest weights are authored values rather than tokens.

Pinned flush to the top-right and bottom-right corners, inset by exactly the badge's own width so both sit inside the avatar's bounds at every size. They scale in position as the avatar resizes and do not move independently.

Ring uses border/default. Each status draws its circle from a chart token, chart/positive for Available, chart/negative for Busy and chart/series steps for the rest, with the glyph on foreground/inverse. Offline inverts that pair, a foreground/inverse circle carrying a foreground/secondary glyph. Swatch colours use chart/series. All resolve separately for light and dark mode.
